useWhen: Designing data structure for new features
Planning how different data objects relate
Validating data model supports required queries

workflow.description: Identify core objects and nouns in your system - what data needs to be stored
Map how entities relate: one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many, foreign keys
Define data fields, types, constraints, defaults, required vs optional
Verify the model can support required queries and identify performance concerns

examples.input: We need to build an e-learning platform with courses, lessons, and student progress tracking. Design the data model.
examples.context: E-learning platform with courses, lessons, students, progress
examples.output:
**ENTITIES**

1. **User** - Students and instructors
2. **Course** - Container for lessons
3. **Lesson** - Individual learning units
4. **Enrollment** - User-course relationship
5. **Progress** - Lesson completion tracking
6. **Quiz** - Assessment questions
7. **QuizAttempt** - Student quiz results

**RELATIONSHIPS**

| Entity A | Relationship | Entity B | Type |
|----------|-------------|----------|------|
| Course | has many | Lesson | 1:N |
| Course | has many | Enrollment | 1:N |
| User | has many | Enrollment | 1:N |
| User | has many | Progress | 1:N |
| Lesson | has many | Progress | 1:N |
| Quiz | belongs to | Lesson | 1:1 |
| Quiz | has many | QuizAttempt | 1:N |
| User | has many | QuizAttempt | 1:N |

**ATTRIBUTES**

*User*
- id (UUID, PK)
- email (string, unique)
- name (string)
- role (enum: student, instructor)
- created_at (timestamp)

*Course*
- id (UUID, PK)
- title (string)
- description (text)
- instructor_id (UUID, FK → User)
- published (boolean)
- created_at (timestamp)

*Lesson*
- id (UUID, PK)
- course_id (UUID, FK → Course)
- title (string)
- content (text)
- order (integer)
- duration_minutes (integer)

*Progress*
- id (UUID, PK)
- user_id (UUID, FK → User)
- lesson_id (UUID, FK → Lesson)
- completed (boolean)
- completed_at (timestamp)

**QUERY VALIDATION**
- Get all lessons for a course ✓
- Get user's progress in a course ✓
- Get courses by instructor ✓
- Calculate completion percentage ✓

examples.input: Design data model for a multi-tenant SaaS with organizations, users, projects, and tasks.
examples.context: Multi-tenant SaaS with organizations as top-level entity
examples.output:
**ENTITIES**

1. **Organization** - Tenant container
2. **User** - Team members
3. **Membership** - User-Org relationship with roles
4. **Project** - Work containers
5. **Task** - Individual work items
6. **Comment** - Task discussions

**RELATIONSHIPS**

| Entity A | Relationship | Entity B | Type |
|----------|-------------|----------|------|
| Organization | has many | Membership | 1:N |
| Organization | has many | Project | 1:N |
| User | has many | Membership | 1:N |
| Project | has many | Task | 1:N |
| Task | has many | Comment | 1:N |
| User | has many | Comment | 1:N |

**ATTRIBUTES**

*Organization*
- id (UUID, PK)
- name (string)
- plan (enum: free, pro, enterprise)
- created_at (timestamp)

*Membership*
- id (UUID, PK)
- user_id (UUID, FK)
- organization_id (UUID, FK)
- role (enum: owner, admin, member)

*Task*
- id (UUID, PK)
- project_id (UUID, FK)
- title (string)
- description (text)
- status (enum: todo, in_progress, done)
- assignee_id (UUID, FK → User)
- due_date (date)

**QUERY VALIDATION**
- Get all projects for org ✓
- Get tasks assigned to user across orgs ✓
- Get org member list ✓
- Filter tasks by status ✓
